desc: Identify the problem as the "Two Pieces" problem from AtCoder.
Note the naive BFS on state graph is too large.
Derive that the answer depends on graph structure (adjacent case, cycle, etc).
Implement BFS from S and from T to compute dS and dT.
Compute the set of vertices on shortest paths from S to T: those with dS[v] + dT[v] == d (d = dS[T]).

For each edge (u,v), compute candidate = dS[u] + dT[v] + 1 and dS[v] + dT[u] + 1, but only if the shortest paths from S to u and from T to v (or vice versa) are internally vertex-disjoint. This can be checked by ensuring no vertex w has dS[w] <= dS[u] and dT[w] <= dT[v] and dS[w] + dT[w] == dS[u] + dT[v]. Equivalently, the pair (dS[u], dT[v]) must be "minimal" among neighbors.
Also consider the case where S and T are adjacent (d=1): answer is 3 if there is a vertex w adjacent to both, else -1.
